heading: Search the answer, not the array
body:
The answer lies between **max(nums)** and **sum(nums)**. Instead of searching for an element, we **binary search the space of possible answers**.

Key insight: if max-sum X works, any value > X also works (monotonic). Find the boundary between feasible and infeasible.

heading: Greedy feasibility check
body:
To test if a candidate max-sum works:

- Pack elements greedily into subarrays
- Start a new subarray when adding the next element would exceed the max
- Return true if total subarrays ≤ k

This runs in O(n), inside O(log sum) binary search iterations.

label: Crux · Python

q: What is the time complexity of this solution?
explain: Greedy check is O(n), binary search does O(log(sum)) iterations → O(n * log(sum))
